title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DARNELL'S SECRET
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Darnell Hughes, a garbage truck driver from Memphis, Tennessee.
Twenty-two years, never missed a pickup.
And he had a secret. Darnell could barely read.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE GLASSES
segments.quote: Literacy is a bridge from misery to hope.
segments.author: Kofi Annan
lines: For thirty years, he had one trick. Oh, I forgot my glasses.
Then his grandson Jaylen brought him a picture book. Pop, read it to me.
At the library, a flyer quoted Kofi Annan, who once led the United Nations:
Literacy is a bridge from misery to hope.
Darnell signed up for Tuesday night reading class.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE WORKOUT
segments.quote: Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body.
segments.author: Richard Steele
lines: His teacher, Mrs. Odom, was seventy-four and tougher than a parking ticket.
On the board, she wrote a line from Richard Steele, an old English writer:
Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body.
So Darnell trained like a boxer. Cereal boxes. Street signs. Ketchup bottles.
His truck partner Ruby begged him to stop reading every sign out loud.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE STUMBLE
segments.quote: Never give in, never give in, never, never, never, never.
segments.author: Winston Churchill
lines: One night, he read out loud and tripped on every third word.
He told Ruby he was done. Ruby quoted Winston Churchill:
Never give in, never give in, never, never, never, never.
That's a lot of nevers, Darnell said. Next Tuesday, he was back. Early.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE FIRST BOOK
segments.quote: Books are the quietest and most constant of friends; they are the most accessible and wisest of counselors, and the most patient of teachers.
segments.author: Charles W. Eliot
lines: By spring, he finished his first whole book. A cowboy story.
Mrs. Odom wrote a line inside from Charles Eliot, a Harvard president:
Books are the quietest and most constant of friends; they are the most accessible and wisest of counselors, and the most patient of teachers.
Darnell got his first library card. It lives in the front of his wallet.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: LEON
segments.quote: The best way to lift one's self up is to help some one else.
segments.author: Booker T. Washington
lines: At work, his buddy Leon was pretending to read a safety form.
Darnell knew that look. He remembered Booker T. Washington:
The best way to lift one's self up is to help some one else.
So he asked Leon to come on Tuesday. Leon said maybe. Leon came.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LAP
segments.quote: Children are made readers on the laps of their parents.
segments.author: Emilie Buchwald
lines: That summer, Jaylen climbed into his lap with the same book.
His wife Tonya had taped a line from the publisher Emilie Buchwald to the fridge:
Children are made readers on the laps of their parents.
And grandparents, she added.
Darnell read every page. He did all the voices. The duck was a hit.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Cross the bridge. Practice daily. Never give in. Befriend books. Lift someone. Read to the little ones.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Cross the bridge. Practice every day. Never give in. Make friends with books. Lift someone up. Read to the little ones.
Me, I read cereal boxes too. That's how I know I need less sugar.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
